title: Normalized completed-coefficient scalar and restriction comparison
statement: Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes with its small pro-etale inverse-image/direct-image adjunction [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $d_A,d_B$ be adic coefficient data with completed ring sheaves $R_W,S_W$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let $c_W:R_W\to S_W$ be ring-sheaf maps satisfying the square $g_*c_X\circ a_R=a_S\circ c_Y$, where $a_R:R_Y\to g_*R_X$ and $a_S:S_Y\to g_*S_X$ are the canonical completed structure maps of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Scalar extension $c^*$ along a ring-sheaf map, its adjunction with restriction of scalars, the derived scalar extension $Lc^*$ computed on K-flat representatives and its cochain counit are those of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. Use ordinary module pullback as inverse image followed by sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with its tensor-unit-normalized adjunction, and the associated unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define the right-adjoint comparison $\operatorname{Res}_{c_Y}\circ g_{*,S}\cong g_{*,R}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}$ from $S_X$-modules to $R_Y$-modules to be identity on every underlying section. Define $\beta^{\mathrm{ord}}:g_S^*c_Y^*\cong c_X^*g_R^*$ to be the inverse of the adjunction conjugate of this right comparison. Apply this map degreewise to complexes. Define $\beta^L:Lg_S^*Lc_Y^*\cong Lc_X^*Lg_R^*$ to be the unique natural isomorphism characterized on every K-flat complex $P$ with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex] and [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] by the equation $\beta^L_{QP};Lc_X^*(\epsilon_{g,R,P});\epsilon_{c_X,g_R^*P}=Lg_S^*(\epsilon_{c_Y,P});\epsilon_{g,S,c_Y^*P};Q(\beta^{\mathrm{ord}}_P)$, where each $\epsilon$ is the canonical derived-to-ordinary cochain counit and semicolon denotes composition in displayed order. No completed structure map is assumed invertible.

proof.text: For the right-adjoint comparison apply Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardCongr to the coefficient-square equality. Both composites are sectionwise pushforward with the composite ring actions. The comparison is identity on every section, and extensionality proves its uniqueness. Conjugating the ordinary adjunctions and mapping complexes gives the existing ordinary comparison.

The pro-etale module inverse image admits its supplied algebraic presentation. Apply the general ringed-topos K-flat preservation theorem to completedModulePullback, using the object and map equations of reductionChange. Apply the independent-coefficient change-of-rings theorem to pbcExtend. Thus both ordinary first legs send the flat-term K-flat representative to a K-flat complex.

Resolve every homotopy object by an independent-coefficient flat-term K-flat complex. Restriction to those homotopy representatives is a localization, using the restriction-localization argument in the existing representative-whiskering module. The complex-to-homotopy quotient restricts to a full essentially surjective functor; combine their fully faithful precomposition functors and transport by quotientCompQhIso.

Form the two composite natural cochain counits. Each is invertible on the representative class: its first factor is the existing derived counit on a K-flat complex and its second factor is the counit on its K-flat image. Compose the left counit isomorphism, the localization of the specified ordinary complex comparison, and the inverse right counit isomorphism. Fully faithful restriction lifts this natural isomorphism uniquely. Cancel the invertible right counit to obtain exactly the prescribed normalization equation and prove uniqueness.
